  "situation": "On 14‑15 April 1999 a convoy of Albanian refugees traveling the Djakovica‑Prizren road was attacked, resulting in roughly 70‑75 deaths and about 100 injuries. NATO initially denied responsibility but later acknowledged that aircraft flying at 15,000 feet had engaged the convoy, relying on naked‑eye visual assessment. NATO pilots and officials believed the vehicles to be military based on shape, movement, and colour, although later analysis indicated a mix of civilian and military vehicles. The attack was suspended when crews became aware of civilian presence. The committee reviewed the incident, noting that the aircrews did not display recklessness sufficient for criminal charges and that NATO had subsequently altered its rules of engagement to require greater caution when civilians are intermingled with military vehicles.",
